simple.meaning: עָלֶה (ʻâleh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a leaf (as coming up on a tree); collectively, foliage.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 3:7. The surrounding context includes land, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָלֶה (H5929) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: עָלֶה (ʻâleh) / H5929 is traced through Genesis 3:7, Genesis 8:11, Leviticus 26:36, Nehemiah 8:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.
The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth.

“ ‘As for those of you who are left, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will put them to flight; and they shall flee, as one flees from the sword. They will fall when no one pursues.

and that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters,”

and that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters,”

and that they should publish and proclaim in all their cities, and in Jerusalem, saying, “Go out to the mountain, and get olive branches, branches of wild olive, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of thick trees, to make temporary shelters,”
Will you harass a driven leaf?
He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water,
He who trusts in his riches will fall,
For you shall be as an oak whose leaf fades,
All of the army of the sky will be dissolved.
You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness,
“ ‘I will utterly consume them, says Yahweh.
For he will be as a tree planted by the waters,

By the river on its bank, on this side and on that side, will grow every tree for food, whose leaf won’t wither, neither will its fruit fail. It will produce new fruit every month, because its waters issue out of the sanctuary. Its fruit will be for food, and its leaf for healing.”

By the river on its bank, on this side and on that side, will grow every tree for food, whose leaf won’t wither, neither will its fruit fail. It will produce new fruit every month, because its waters issue out of the sanctuary. Its fruit will be for food, and its leaf for healing.”

definitions.short: a leaf (as coming up on a tree); collectively, foliage
definitions.full: H5929. aleh עָלֶה noun masculine leaf, leafage (see עלה Qal 4 ; — ׳ע Lev 26:36 +; construct עֲלֵה Gen 3:7 ; 8:11 ; suffix עָלֵהוּ Jer 17:8 +; plural construct עֲלֵי Neh 8:15 +; suffix עֶלֶהָ Isa 1:30 ; — leaf, leafage , of various trees Gen 3:7 ; 8:11 ; Neh 8:15 (5 t. in verse); green Jer 17:8 , flourishing Prov 11:28 ; but usually fading Isa 1:30 ; 34:4 ; 64:5 ; Jer 8:13 ; Ezek 47:12 ; Psa 1:3 ; driven leaf Lev 26:36 ; Job 13:25 ; לִתְרוּפָה עלה leaf for healing Ezek 47:12 .
